items.title: 68003_Eddie Sauter oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] I saw Stokowski conduct a few years before he died... There was no question that he was fully in control of that orchestra.

ctx.x: There's a story of one percussionist who at one point got out a spy glass and he stopped the orchestra and said, what are you doing. He said I'm trying to find your beat. I guess he lost his job too.
I saw Stokowski conduct a few years before he died, that's

when he had the American Symphony, in the early seventies, and by that time he was close to ninety and his conducting was the same way. There was a definite beat but it was very small strokes, and you really had to watch him closely, but it was still there. There was no question about it. There was no question that he was fully in control of that orchestra.
